title: Fractal cosmology: the infinite in both directions
statement: The canon presents a spatially self-similar cosmos: the stars and planets are the atoms of a larger living being, the atoms of our bodies hold inhabited worlds, and in both directions the structure is infinite — with the compressed physical corollary that time runs inversely to the mass-scale of the form of life; the corpus adopts this picture as the canon's cosmological frame, and keeps the article's dialogue with modern physics as a separate, speculative layer outside this record.

includes: The canonical picture, which is explicit: scale self-similarity in both directions, delivered twice in the second message and emblematized ('as it is above, so it is below') in the first
The time-mass corollary as the canon states it, at the canon's level of statement
The frame function: this is the cosmological premise other corpus developments (macrobiology above all) ride on
excludes: The article's engagement with modern physics (scale relativity, hierarchy problem adjacencies), which is its own speculative development and not this record's content
Any claim that mainstream cosmology supports scale self-similarity; observational cosmology's homogeneity results stand against it and are recorded
Numerical or dimensional elaboration beyond the canon's statements
The emblem's history, which is iconography, not cosmology

source_references.locator: The Yahweh-delivered scale passages (the field teaching and the base teaching): stars as atoms of a being, atoms as worlds, 'in both directions, it is infinite'; the time-mass sentence
TBWTT-3:288 (the emblem: 'as it is above, so it is below'); TBWTT-5:57 (the disease-of-the-universe passage the Explainer reads in this frame)
The mathematical vocabulary of self-similarity the corpus borrows for its name — borrowed as vocabulary, not as endorsement

alternatives.statement: Large-scale structure surveys show the universe transitioning to statistical homogeneity; unbounded self-similarity upward is observationally disfavored.
Worlds-within-atoms is a recurring speculative image (ancient atomism to modern fiction); the canon's version is the genre, not a cosmology.
Quantum mechanics gives atoms a structure nothing like planetary systems; the downward direction fails on known physics.

revision_triggers: The canon's fuller context changes the scale-picture or the time-mass statement.
Public prose begins claiming mainstream-physics support, which this record excludes.
The corpus's physics-dialogue layer produces a result that should be recorded as its own claim.
Claim woh-claim-0020 is revised in a way that affects the provenance of the scale passages.
